## Purpose and Scope

This Reference Architecture Document (RAD) provides illustrative patterns and logical component descriptions for realizing the Application Security Testing capability within the enterprise development pipeline. It is the primary consumption point for the following ABBs:

- [GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SAST-2.7.07 — Static Application Security Testing](../abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SAST-2.7.07.md)
- [GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DAST-2.7.08 — Dynamic Application Security Testing](../abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DAST-2.7.08.md)
- [GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IAST-2.7.09 — Interactive Application Security Testing](../abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IAST-2.7.09.md)
- [GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SCA-2.7.10 — Software Composition Analysis](../abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SCA-2.7.10.md)
- [GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IMGSC-2.7.13 — Container Image Scanning](../abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IMGSC-2.7.13.md)

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-APP-RA-APPSEC-TESTING-2.7.28.md#capability-domain-boundary]

### Capability Domain Boundary

Application Security Testing operates within the CI/CD pipeline, from commit through pre-production deployment. Its boundary ends at the point where an artifact is promoted to production — runtime protection is handled by the Web Application Protection (WAF/RASP) and Runtime Container Security capabilities.

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-APP-RA-APPSEC-TESTING-2.7.28.md#control-responsibility-matrix]

### Control Responsibility Matrix

| Activity | Platform Engineering | Security Architecture | Development Teams |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pipeline gate configuration | **Owns** | Advises | Informs |
| Finding triage and remediation | Supports | Advises | **Owns** |
| Rule and policy maintenance | Supports | **Owns** | Informs |
| Exception approval | — | **Owns** | Requests |
page_texts.8:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-APP-RA-APPSEC-TESTING-2.7.28.md#pipeline-control-outcome-requirement]

### Pipeline Control Outcome Requirement

Security testing capabilities defined in this document SHALL be enforced in CI/CD before merge and pre-production promotion, including SAST, SCA, dependency integrity verification, container image scanning, and SBOM generation. The delivery mechanism (for example, template-driven paved roads, centralized policy engines, or equivalent controls) is a Platform Engineering design decision.

Development teams retain responsibility for:

- Remediating findings attributed to their code and dependencies
- Requesting exceptions through the Security Architecture–owned exception process
- Providing a deployed test environment target for DAST execution
- Defining and maintaining the test-environment access credentials used by DAST (via the Secrets Management capability)

### Logical Components

| Component | Type | Architectural Role |
|---|---|---|
| SAST Engine | ABB Realization — GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SAST-2.7.07 | Source code analysis at commit/PR |
| SCA Engine | ABB Realization — GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SCA-2.7.10 | Dependency vulnerability and license analysis |
| Image Scanner | ABB Realization — GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IMGSC-2.7.13 | Container image vulnerability and policy scan |
| DAST Engine | ABB Realization — GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DAST-2.7.08 | Black-box testing of deployed test instance |
| IAST Agent | ABB Realization — GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IAST-2.7.09 | Optional in-process testing instrumentation |
| Finding Aggregator | Logical Service | Normalizes findings from multiple tools into unified severity model |
| Gate Decision Logic | Pipeline Integration | Enforces promotion/block decisions based on finding severity thresholds |

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-APP-RA-APPSEC-TESTING-2.7.28.md#pattern-1-shift-left-static-and-composition-analysis]

### Pattern 1: Shift-Left Static and Composition Analysis

**When to use**: At every code commit or pull request, before merge.

**Logical flow**:

1. Developer pushes code or opens a pull request
2. SAST engine analyzes source code for vulnerability patterns
3. SCA engine analyzes dependency manifest for known vulnerabilities and license issues
4. Findings are aggregated and evaluated against gate thresholds
5. Developer receives findings in the code review interface; merge is blocked if threshold is exceeded

**Illustrative technology class**: Static analysis engine with pull request integration; dependency scanning integrated with package manager
page_texts.14:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-APP-RA-APPSEC-TESTING-2.7.28.md#pattern-2-container-gate-at-build]

### Pattern 2: Container Gate at Build

**When to use**: After every successful application build that produces a container image.

**Logical flow**:

1. Build pipeline produces a container image
2. Image scanner evaluates all layers for known vulnerabilities and policy violations
3. Passing images receive a signed attestation
4. Admission control in the deployment environment verifies attestation before scheduling

**Illustrative technology class**: Container image scanning service integrated with registry; policy engine with admission webhook
page_texts.15:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-APP-RA-APPSEC-TESTING-2.7.28.md#pattern-3-dynamic-testing-in-pre-production]

### Pattern 3: Dynamic Testing in Pre-Production

**When to use**: After successful deployment to a representative test environment.

**Logical flow**:

1. Application is deployed to test environment
2. DAST engine probes application endpoints
3. Optional: IAST agent instruments the application during concurrent functional test execution
4. Combined findings are evaluated against pre-production promotion gate
5. Promotion to production is blocked if high/critical findings are unresolved

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-APP-RA-APPSEC-TESTING-2.7.28.md#deployment-context-considerations]

## Deployment Context Considerations

| Context | Architectural Consideration |
|---|---|
| Cloud-native (containerized) | Image scanning and admission control are first-class pipeline gates; cloud-native registry integration simplifies attestation |
| Hybrid (mixed containerized and VM-based) | DAST and SAST/SCA patterns apply across both; image scanning applies only to containerized components |
| Shared pipeline platform | Finding aggregation must account for multi-team, multi-application result sets; namespace isolation in the aggregator is required |

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-APP-RA-APPSEC-TESTING-2.7.28.md#constraints-and-exceptions]

## Constraints and Exceptions

- IAST instrumentation is optional per GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-IAST-2.7.09; teams choosing not to implement IAST must achieve equivalent coverage through SAST + DAST.
- Pipeline performance requirements may necessitate asynchronous execution of DAST; gate decisions must define how asynchronous results are handled.
- False positive suppression and exception processes must be defined before gates are enforced in production pipelines.
